title: WPSS/1408/2016 of Anuj Vij Vs Food Corporation Of India Ltd AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.1408/16
Honíble Rajiv Sharma, J.
 Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate for
the petitioner.
 Mr. Yogesh Pande, Advocate, for the
respondents.
 Petitioner participated in the
selection process for the post of Assistant
Grade-II (Hindi). He was required to file
one-year Experience Certificate of
Translation from Hindi to English and
vice versa.
 In the experience certificate dated
20.2.2015 submitted by the petitioner, it
is stated that he has worked in the
capacity of ëHindi Translatorí from 1st
January, 2014 to 15th February, 2015.
 The suitability of the petitioner was
adjudged. He was found meritorious.
However, the appointment letter was not
issued to the petitioner on the ground
that he did not possess the requisite
experience of Translation from English to
Hindi and Vice-Versa.
 Attention of the Court has been
drawn to Page No.29 of the paper book,
according to which, the candidates, in
Paper-IV, were required to translate two
passages, one each from Hindi to English
and Vice-Versa, and two Essays each in
Hindi and English. Duration of the
examination was 90 minutes.
 At page no.33 of the paper book, it
is also stated that a candidate, who has
scored higher marks in Paper-IV of
Written Test, will be placed above the
other candidates.
 Petitioner was placed above other
candidates on the basis of securing
higher marks in Paper-IV.

Petitioner sought information under
the Right to Information Act. He was
informed vide order dated 3.8.2016 that
the experience certificate, attached by
him, only indicates his experience of
Hindi Translation, and not Vice Versa.
 The respondents have adopted a
very hyper-technical approach. Petitioner
had undertaken the Translation of Hindi
to English as well as English to Hindi and
qualified the same.
Thus, in view of the observations
and discussions made hereinabove, it is
hereby declared that the petitioner had
the requisite qualification, as laid down
in the advertisement published in the
year 2015. The petition is, accordingly,
allowed. Order dated 3.8.2016 (Annexure
No.CA3 to the counter affidavit) is
quashed and set aside. The respondents
are directed to offer appointment letter to
the petitioner within three weeks from
today.
 All pending applications stand
disposed of in the above terms.
